newsitem.title: UK: Euro stocks retreat after Dow falls again.
newsitem.headline: Euro stocks retreat after Dow falls again.

text.p: European shares reeled on Thursday after Wall Street suffered another big loss on fears that U.S. interest rates may rise again soon.
The Dow Jones average of leading U.S. shares slid 94 points to 6,517.01 on Wednesday.

Trade was thin and nervous ahead of Friday's crucial U.S. non-farm payrolls figures which could signal if and when rates will rise again to counter the threat of inflation in the world's biggest economy.
Higher U.S. rates could undermine Wall Street, which has shed some 400 points since the U.S. Federal Reserve nudged rates higher last week.
If Wall Street slides further, this would be bad news for other leading bourses, despite recent talk that they might be going their own way, moving independently from Wall Street.
"No one wants to be heroic ahead of the (U.S. jobs) data," a share trader in London said.
London's FTSE 100 index of blue-chip shares was down 27.6 points, or 0.65 percent, at 4,209.0 by 0930 gmt, when in Paris the CAC 40 index was down 19.04 points, or 0.75 percent, at 2,511.24.

Germany's DAX index, which closed floor trade before Wall Street opened on Wednesday, was down around 100 points, or three percent, although most of the losses reflected the index factoring in the U.S. falls.

Nerves in Frankfurt, which has been under greater pressure than other European bourses, remained on edge after the fresh drop on Wall Street and investors braced themselves to see what the afternoon would bring.
"It's just nerves, nerves and more nerves here," said a Frankfurt trader. "There is no hope of us decoupling from the U.S."
Dealers said that while German shares should not be tracking the U.S. market on the basis of economic fundamentals, the psychological impact of Wall Street's decline was immense.
"It's clear we are at a different stage here in the economic cycle -- no one is talking about a German rate hike today. But it still all depends on Wall Street," a dealer said.
The Bundesbank's policy-making council meeting on Thursday morning will attract its usual measure of attention but economists were not expecting the central bank to make any move on rates.
In London, domestic British political concerns were expected to be thrust back into the spotlight with the release of the opposition Labour Party's manifesto.
Labour is well ahead in the opinion polls and widely expected to form the next government after the May 1 general election. The ruling Conservatives launched their manifesto on Wednesday.
"People didn't react much to the Conservative manifesto but the Labour one will be closer watched," a dealer said. "It's going to add further to the uncertainty, I'm afraid."
French stocks were pressured by Wall Street's fall and Renault shares were particularly weak, falling 2.4 percent to 128 francs after unions called for work stoppages on Friday.
In currencies, the dollar was firmer against the mark and flirting with 123 yen in early European trade, though it then slipped from its highest levels.
Analysts said further gains were likely to be capped ahead of U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin's visit to Japan and the U.S. jobs data on Friday.

"The market is somewhat on hold and it is pretty unlikely that we will break out of current trading ranges ahead of these two events," said Klaus Baader, senior currency economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.

Analysts said dollar markets were on tenterhooks ahead of Rubin's visit to Japan after comments earlier this week on Japan's trade surplus with the United States, which rose in February for the first time in two years, knocked the dollar to a low of 121.35 yen and re-focused attention on the gap.
CURRENCIES AT 0930 GMT
The dollar was at 1.6724 marks and 122.77 yen, compared with 1.6713 and 122.70 in late European trade on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0930 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index fell by 27.6 points to 4,209.0.
PARIS - The CAC-40 dropped 19.04 points to 2,511.24.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index fell 96.41 to 3,205.50. In electronic trade, the IBIS index was down 7.13 points at 3,203.81.
PRECIOUS METALS AT 0930 GMT
Gold fixed at $349.10, compared with Wednesday's closing price in London of $351.35 an ounce.
